entities.summary: Angelo Barbarigo (1350-1418) was a Roman Catholic Cardinal who played a pivotal role in shaping the Church's response to the Black Death. During his tenure as papal legate, he worked closely with Emperor Sigismund to establish quarantine protocols and coordinate relief efforts in affected regions. His leadership during this crisis cemented his reputation as a shrewd politician and earned him a place among the most influential Cardinals of his era. Barbarigo's contributions to the Church's response to the pandemic have been recognized as a turning point in the history of medical ethics, influencing the development of quarantine policies for centuries to come.
